title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
authors: S. Archana, Aditi Das, Venkat Abhignan, R. Muthuganesan
abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.
summary: This work analyzes the resilience of quantum resources, specifically the GHZ state, used in controlled quantum teleportation under various noise models. By comparing multipartite discord, entanglement, and CQT fidelity, the authors show that these measures reveal distinct aspects of robustness. The findings emphasize that operational performance, measured by fidelity, is key to assessing practical quantum advantage.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the performance of controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) and the utility of quantum resources degrade when subjected to various types of noise.
main_result: It demonstrates that different quantum correlation measures (discord, concurrence, entanglement) exhibit distinct robustness profiles, and that operational fidelity (CQT fidelity) is a more reliable indicator of resource usefulness than entanglement measures alone.
method: The study uses the Kraus-operator formalism to model noisy evolution on a three-qubit GHZ state and compares the resulting state using multiple quantum correlation diagnostics.
model_or_system: The core system is the three-qubit GHZ state used as a resource for the Controlled Quantum Teleportation (CQT) protocol, analyzed under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise.
key_observables: Multipartite quantum discord, Genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), Localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity.
important_parameters: Noise strength parameters (e.g., $p$), and the comparison against the classical threshold ($2/3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the Kraus-operator formalism to model the noisy channels and that the CQT protocol structure remains valid.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic flow of the CQT protocol and show the dependence of CQT fidelity on noise strength for different noise configurations.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the CQT protocol and the noisy GHZ resource. It then analyzes the resource robustness using various correlation measures, culminating in a comparison showing the operational relevance of LE versus the mathematical persistence of discord.
why_interesting: The detailed comparison between different correlation measures (discord vs. entanglement) and the operational fidelity provides crucial guidelines for designing robust quantum communication protocols in realistic noisy environments.

Alice, Bob, and Charlie hold qubits 1, 2, and 3 of the shared resource 𝜌𝐺𝐻𝑍, respectively using a noisy three-qubit quantum channel. Alice performs the sender-side Bell measurement between the input state and qubit 1, Charlie performs the controller measurement on qubit 3, and Bob applies the corresponding conditional operation to qubit 2 to obtain the output state 𝜌out. The shared three-qubit channel is subject to bit-flip (BF), phase-flip (PF), depolarising (DP), and amplitude-damping (AD) noise.

Fig. 4. Quantum discord as a function of the noise strength 𝑝under amplitude-damping (ADC), bit-flip (BF), phase-flip (PF) and depolarizing (DP) noise acting on the qubits.

Fig. 4 shows how the multipartite discord of the noisy GHZ state varies with the noise strength 𝑝for the four different noise channels. Amplitude damping and bit-flip yield the slowest decay of discord and only at large noise parameters 𝑝does discord approach zero. The bit-flip noise curves exhibit a freezing phenomenon, with the discord remaining at its maximum value up to a finite noise strength of 𝑝≈0.20 when noise acts on the receiver and controller qubits [Fig. 4(a)] and 𝑝≈0.10 when all qubits are subjected to noise [Fig. 4(b)].
